prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Context: Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) NextGen/National Airspace System (NAS); National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Airspace Technology Demonstrations 3 (ATD-3). Actors: FAA managers/controllers, airline air traffic control (ATC) coordinators/dispatchers, aircraft/operators/pilots/crews, American Airlines, public/industry/air traffic management (ATM) stakeholders. Aids: flight management systems, onboard weather radar. Traffic Management Initiatives (TMIs) divert/meter; managers designate Flow Constrained Areas (FCAs). Severe Weather Avoidance Plans (SWAP)=Playbook routes, 2–8-hour horizon. Dispatchers must file ≥45 minutes pre-pushback. Collaborative Trajectory Options Program (CTOP) receives operator route/delay preferences; no postdeparture optimization. Crews coordinate alternatives with controllers/dispatchers; conflict avoidance requires controller coordination. NASA Dynamic Weather Routes (DWR), extending Direct-To, continuously analyzes flights ≥10,000 ft using tracks/plans/weather/airspace/traffic. Maneuver Start Point (MSP): adjustable coordination delay (default five minutes) or high-altitude entry (Fort Worth Center=ZFW: FL240); snaps within 10 nmi. Return Capture Fix (RCF; Capture fix): last fix inside limit rectangle (~200 nmi beyond ZFW), or before Standard Terminal Arrival Route (STAR). Historical direct-clearance polygons: Future ATM Concept Evaluation Tool (FACET)/National Airspace System Constraint Evaluation and Notification Tool (NASCENT); city-pair selection possible. Wind-corrected savings threshold: user-defined, default five minutes. Weather/optional-traffic avoidance inserts one/two minimum-delay auxiliary waypoints (fix-radial-distance; optional named-fix snapping). Both trajectories checked for congestion/Special Use Airspace (SUA); polygon avoidance supports nonweather obstacles. Weather/traffic conflicts reject trial plans; search continues. DWR sends qualifying advisories to responsible users’ savings-ordered DWR list; retains latest qualifiers. Indicators: TR=traffic minutes-to-conflict; SC=sector congestion; WX=weather; R=active Route TMI. Display: dashed-white advisory, MSP/RCF/auxiliary waypoints; bottom current/advisory routes and Capture fix menu & flying time savings; right current/advisory congestion panels: red=airborne-only, yellow=proposed-departure contributions. Users point/click/drag MSP, RCF, waypoint

U0117: Research indicates that digital communication of proposed DWR routes between ATC and the flight deck combined with on-board display of proposed route, would allow much faster review and approval of the DWR route [4] [5]. 4.1 CONVECTIVE WEATHER MODEL DWR utilizes convective weather forecast data from FAA’s Corridor Integrated Weather System (CIWS) and Convective Weather Avoidance Model (CWAM) [15-17] to identify routes that will avoid convective cells.
U0118: CIWS forecasts the growth, decay, and movement of convective weather and updates every 5 minutes with a 2-hour look-ahead time in 5-minute increments (see Figure 7).
U0119: This allows DWR to identify alternative routes that are predicted to remain clear of weather at the time the flight is calculated to pass the cell(s).
U0120: Figure 7: CIWS and CWAM Forecast Sample Figure 8: CIWS cell and corresponding 60, 70, & 80% CWAM polygons CWAM identifies boundaries around convective cells that represent the distance by which flight crews are expected to deviate around the cell [15][16][17].
U0121: The boundary polygon, known as a Weather Avoidance Field (WAF), represents the probability a flight crew will deviate around the cell based on storm intensity, echo tops, and look-ahead time.
U0122: A WAF is identified by the probability that a given percentage of pilots would deviate around the storm at that distance based on extensive historical data.
U0123: For a given weather cell and altitude, 70% of WAF polygons are generally smaller with their boundaries closer to the weather cells than are 60% WAF polygons (see Figure 8).
U0124: WAF polygons (60, 70, and 80%) are identified for every 5-minute CWIS forecast interval out to 2 hours, at flight levels ranging from FL250 to FL450 in 1,000’ increments.
U0125: DWR normally utilizes 70% WAF polygons when generating route advisories, but the default WAF parameter can be selected at system start up. 4.2 CONVECTIVE CELL GAP DETECTION AND REJECTION DWR logic includes gap detection and rejection logic to ensure a gap is large enough to safely route aircraft.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
